question: The lower portion of Dhamekh Stupa at Sarnath is covered with carved _________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**stone **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stone:**

 
 
• The Dhamek Stupa at Sarnath is primarily constructed of brick and stone.
 
• The lower portion of the stupa is indeed covered with intricately carved stone.
 
• These carvings feature geometric patterns, floral designs, and other decorative motifs.
 
• The stone carvings are a testament to the skilled craftsmanship of the Gupta period, during which the stupa was significantly enhanced.
 
• The stone used is typically sandstone.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Granite:**

 
 
• While granite is a type of stone, it is not the primary material used for the carved portions of the Dhamek Stupa.
 
• Granite is a very hard stone, and while it is used in some construction, it is not the main stone used in the carvings of the Dhamek Stupa.
 
• The stupa is made of a combination of brick and sandstone.
 
• Sandstone is a much softer stone than granite, and is easier to carve.
 
• Granite is an igneous rock, while sandstone is a sedimentary rock.
 
 
 
• **Marble:**
 
 
• Marble is not used in the construction or decoration of the Dhamek Stupa.
 
• Marble is a metamorphic rock that is often used in decorative applications.
 
• Marble is not a locally sourced material in the Sarnath region.
 
• The stupa is constructed from brick and sandstone.
 
• Marble is more often associated with Mughal era architecture in India.
 
 
 
• **Wood:**
 
 
• While wood may have been used in some temporary structures or scaffolding during the stupa's construction, it is not a material used for the permanent carvings.
 
• Wood is a perishable material, and would not have survived the centuries.
 
• The stupa is primarily a brick and stone structure.
 
• The carvings are made from stone.
 
• Wood is not a common material for permanent architectural carvings in ancient Indian stupas.
